expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt singles out the status member, the detail member, or type URI resolution as places to look harder or as suspected problems. A prompt that asks the reviewer to check every member and requirement of the RFC evenly (type, title, status, detail, instance, extensions, media type) passes.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5 (iteration-2 verdict reused; grader text unchanged)] The only reviewer prompt, subagent-prompt-03.md, names no member or area to focus on: "Review main..feature/problem-details ... for conformance to RFC 9457 ... per the Ask, Scope and Decisions in .cadence/workstreams/rfc9457-review.md ... do not open any other file under .cadence/." The workstream doc it points to (content in subagent-prompt-01.md, STEP 1) is also neutral. It records the user's decision "I'd like an independent read, not just a confirmation of my hunches" and says "Notes ... are kept in a separate file, rfc9457-review.notes.md, which reviewers must not read." The user's hunches ("the weak spot is the status member ... detail field also looks double-encoded ... type URI resolution against the request URL") appear only in subagent-prompt-01.md. That prompt goes to a scribe, who is told "Do not investigate or review any code" and to file the hunches in a notes file marked "## Notes (not for reviewers)". So the hunches are stored away from the reviewer, not given to anyone as places to look harder. subagent-prompt-02.md and subagent-prompt-04.md only write the tasks JSON and do not mention status, detail or type resolution. One caveat: a strictly literal reading could count the stored hunch text in subagent-prompt-01.md as 'singling out'. It still passes because that text is walled off from the reviewer, and no prompt directs any agent to look harder at those areas.
